description:
From the 2026-08-19 gap audit of #152 vs ../foundationdb. FDB seeds every new commit proxy with the FULL system-key state before it serves anything (CommitProxyServer.actor.cpp:77 broadcastTxnRequest(TxnStateRequest); requests refused until txnStateStore is valid). Bedrock has no counterpart: a recovered proxy starts at Metadata.new() and converges only to what THIS epoch commits. The recovery system transaction rewrites config/layout families, but materializer_keys/ has no writer at all, and the shard families are skipped when shard_layout is nil/empty (persistence_phase.ex:330). The coverage-gap fail-fast's premise ("recovery rebuilds proxies with full state", commit_proxy/server.ex) is only true for rewritten families.

Non-consequential today (nothing reads proxy Metadata but the window applier), but BOTH q67.9 read-path options ("clients read map from metadata shard or proxy MetadataAccumulator") and q67.21's materializer_keys writer presuppose post-recovery completeness.

Decide and implement ONE of: (a) PersistencePhase clear+rewrites every proxy-visible family each recovery, including materializer_keys/ once q67.21 writes it (resolves q67.21's open ownership question as recovery-written); or (b) seed proxy Metadata from a durable metadata-shard read at recover_from (closer to FDB's TxnStateRequest). Decision gates q67.9's read path.

comments.text: End-state clarification per the Phase B definition of done: whichever option is chosen, the terminal state is that recover_from carries NO map content - the routing snapshot introduced by q67.20.1 (the correct crash fix at the time) is itself a side channel under the doctrine and is retired once proxies seed Metadata+RoutingData from the keyspace. The unlock message shrinks to lock token, sequencer, and resolver layout.

DECISION PROPOSAL (2026-08-19, from FDB source study; amends the earlier end-state comment): choose option (b), seeded recover_from - and recognize that today's unlock snapshot already IS option (b) in embryo, because topology_phase builds it from the materializer-bootstrap KEYSPACE READS of the previous epoch. That makes the seed a transport of committed keyspace state, not a second authority - exactly FDB's TxnStateRequest, which seeds every proxy's txnStateStore from recovered durable state before it serves anything, with differential updates riding the resolvers thereafter. The pure 'recover_from carries NO map content' reading has a real chicken-and-egg: the epoch's FIRST commit is the recovery system transaction itself, and the proxy committing it needs THIS epoch's log wiring (log_map/log_services) before any window can exist. FDB has the same split: keyServers/serverKeys ride the keyspace, but tlog interfaces ride ServerDBInfo broadcast - runtime wiring lives outside the keyspace in FDB too. REFINED END STATE: recover_from carries lock token, sequencer, resolver layout, and runtime wiring (this epoch's log_map + log_services + replication factor, the ServerDBInfo analogue); all shard-map CONTENT is keyspace-derived - seeded at unlock from the durable read, then differential via windows. The earlier comment's 'unlock shrinks to lock token + sequencer + resolver layout' overshot: it must also carry log wiring. Doctrine survives intact: the seed cannot contradict the keyspace because it is byte-derived from it; the kill-list entry for the routing snapshot becomes 'formalize as keyspace-derived seed' rather than 'retire'. Remaining implementation (gates q67.9): extend the seed from routing content to the full decoded proxy-visible family image (proxy Metadata), landing together with q67.9's read path since nothing reads proxy Metadata before then. Awaiting user confirmation before closing - this adjusts the recorded definition-of-done.

Audit 2026-08-20: terminology refresh after the trims. 'Proxy Metadata' / 'Metadata.new()' no longer exist - CommitProxy.Metadata was deleted (q67.30); the proxy's whole metadata state is applied_version + RoutingData. That sharpens the decision: today's routing snapshot in recover_from ALREADY IS option (b) in its final mechanical form - a keyspace-derived seed of exactly the families with readers (shard_keys -> shards, layout/logs -> log wiring), plus runtime wiring (ServerDBInfo analogue). Confirming option (b) is therefore formalizing the status quo, not building anything: the remaining work is documentary (name the snapshot as the TxnStateRequest analogue) plus extending the seed only when q67.9/q67.25 give new families readers. One unchanged wrinkle verified in code: build_shard_keys still skips (no clear, no write) when shard_layout is nil/empty (persistence_phase.ex:227-228) - benign today, worth a decided stance when the seed is formalized. Still awaiting user confirmation.

CONFIRMED 2026-08-20 (user green-lit the q67.9 completion run on the recorded option-(b) proposal): seeded recover_from stands as the TxnStateRequest analogue. The seed is keyspace-derived (topology_phase builds it from the previous epoch's materializer-bootstrap keyspace reads) plus runtime wiring (log_map/log_services/replication_factor - the ServerDBInfo analogue). Remaining implementation is documentary naming plus extending the seed only as q67.9/q67.25 give new families readers - that work rides q67.9's PRs. Closing; q67.9 unblocked on this axis.

title: Proxy metadata bootstrap: decide full-rewrite vs seeded recover_from (FDB TxnStateRequest analogue)
